title: The Session Manager Field Manual
summary: A tab-by-tab operator's guide to Claude Code Session Manager — what each surface is for, the one thing people get wrong about it, and the workflow that makes it pay for itself.

chapters.title: Getting Started — the 10-minute setup
chapters.blurb: Install, open your first project tab, and understand the one idea the whole app is built on: a TAB is a project, a SESSION is a unit of work.

chapters.title: Epics & Sessions — Terminal and Chat are one session
chapters.blurb: Why an Epic is a tagged Claude session, how Agent + Mission ground it, and why switching between Terminal and Chat never loses your context.

chapters.title: File Explorer — one browser, two starting points
chapters.blurb: Why the same tab opens to your home folder from Home but your active project from a Tab, the autosave + dirty-state editor pane, and switching projects without leaving it.

chapters.title: Scheduler — author once, run around your token window
chapters.blurb: Writing a PRD that actually completes, how the queue picks work, auto-pause on rate limits, and reading a job parked in needs_review.

chapters.title: Settings & Scopes — editing the substrate, not the conversation
chapters.blurb: The User/Project/Local scope model, why a Settings edit changes every Epic in scope rather than just the one you're in, and when to reach for a Tag or Agent instead.

chapters.title: MCP Servers — registering tools, and proving they actually connected
chapters.blurb: Editing ~/.claude.json and .mcp.json safely, and the live-probe workflow that catches a server that looks configured but never actually connects.

chapters.title: Permissions — stop the interruptions, don't disable the guardrail
chapters.blurb: Allow/deny/ask rules, the three scopes, the mistake people make with Project scope, and using fewer-permission-prompts to build the allowlist for you.

chapters.title: Agent Library — authoring the "who" of an Epic
chapters.blurb: Building focused personas instead of repeating instructions in every prompt, how a persona's model field picks --model, and the project-override mistake that makes an edit look like it did nothing.

chapters.title: System Prompt — editing the CLI's own house rules, machine-wide
chapters.blurb: The one file this tab actually writes — ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md — why there's no scope switcher, and editing an @-import as the real file it is, not a preview.

chapters.title: Skills — what auto-fires, what you type, and where it lives
chapters.blurb: Telling a Skill apart from a Slash Command, why scope matters before you touch Toggle or Remove, and finding this project's own dev skillset in the Library.

chapters.title: Plugins — the Installed inspector and the Library catalog
chapters.blurb: Why Installed is read-only by design, how Library's Install button actually runs claude plugin install for you, and where this project's own dev skillset comes from.

chapters.title: Home & Project Brief — the cockpit's dashboard
chapters.blurb: How the Home tab's cross-project dashboard and a project's self-maintaining Brief document actually work, and the daily workflow that gets the most out of both.

chapters.title: Hooks — edit the CLI's own shell-outs, safely
chapters.blurb: A guide to the Hooks tab's event editor, scope merging, and the test-fire workflow for safely verifying a hook command before it runs for real.

chapters.title: Tag Library — the mission that ships with every Epic
chapters.blurb: How a tag's opening framing and /develop eagerness shape every Epic that carries it, and the one relationship on this page you can actually edit.

chapters.title: Host on Bilko.run — publishing this project's page, gated for real
chapters.blurb: The free Prepare Bundle / gated Publish two-stage pipeline, hosting more than one page under one listing, and reading a gate failure without guessing.

chapters.title: History — where your Claude time and money went
chapters.blurb: How to read the History dashboard's cost/token/tool analytics and catch a runaway-spend project before the bill does — it's not a session browser.

chapters.title: Memory Clusters — what an agent has actually been remembering
chapters.blurb: How the Memory tab's Clusters view groups a project's saved memory notes into themes, why it's a cost-gated periodic report rather than a live view, and how to read an empty result.

chapters.title: Usage — reading the 5-hour window before it reads you
chapters.blurb: How the 5-hour and weekly usage meters work, where the numbers come from, and tuning the session slot pool so the Scheduler pausing on a rate limit never surprises you.

chapters.title: Voice Input — dictate into any session, offline
chapters.blurb: How the local Silero VAD + Moonshine speech pipeline actually works, the auto-submit timer people talk over, and the workflow that makes dictation faster than typing.

chapters.title: Plans & Tasks — reading what the agent already told you
chapters.blurb: How Session Manager surfaces an agent's live to-do list and plan revisions straight from the transcript, and the footer chip that replaced the old Tasks tab.

chapters.title: Simple Mode — the chrome-free single-terminal cockpit
chapters.blurb: What --simple actually boots (one skip-perms terminal, no nav or config surface), why persisted tabs and Epics never appear there, and when to reach for it instead of the full app.
